human.problem: The joke 'when MY phone says “You have arrived,” I'm staring at an empty parking lot' gives Papa Dorin a phone and has him driving to parking lots. In the backstory, he lives alone on a cookie planet just big enough for his bakery. papa-dorin.md lets him use phones and traffic for comparisons and lets jokes make up small habits around his bakery. It also says he never adds anything new to his world. It doesn't say whether a joke can claim a first-person everyday-life experience outside the bakery.
human.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes describe himself personally using everyday adult things like a phone, GPS or driving, or should those stay as general comparisons (for example, 'when your phone says...')?
